swap.evidence: Products swapped in: a city bike-share reservation and a camera-equipment hire shop. Surviving unchanged: masthead (name in bold body type plus stock wrench outline), pale ground with white bordered cards, forest-green filled button, the card layout with an icon tile, badge chips, the calendar and session radio cards. Bound to this product: only the copy (deposits, 'Open' sessions, the desk phone number, volunteer phrasing). With the name and copy hidden, a reader could not tell this is a volunteer-run tool library.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a community / sharing-economy service: near-white or pale green ground, one green 'eco/community' accent, rounded white cards, a friendly sans, line icons. Predicted opposite: bold workshop look (black and safety yellow, stencil type, pegboard). The render matches the default on ground, accent hue, card treatment, face and icon. The green is justified in DESIGN.md as the membership-card green, but nothing on screen shows that card, so it reads as the category green.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online reservation for a neighbourhood toy library run by parents'. Predicted choices: pale ground, one green or teal accent, card grid with a placeholder icon per item, date picker, radio slots, a check-and-confirm form. Overlap: all identity-carrying choices; only the tool icon would change to a toy.

evidence: All three tests fail on identity-carrying elements: masthead is name-in-body-type plus stock wrench; the same wrench placeholder fills every tool thumbnail; the palette and card frame are the category default.
Product-bound content exists (Open-session calendar, availability-from badges, deposit on every card, volunteer copy) but sits on a portable frame (anchor 1).

attributes.x_evidence: Deposit on every card; 'Available from' badges; concrete specs (13 mm keyless, 1.7 kg); one filled action per page; error summary linking to fields.
attributes.y_evidence: Little pulls toward corporate; the generic green-and-white card frame is neutral rather than corporate.

attributes.x_evidence: Copy only: 'Fernhill Tool Library is run by volunteers', 'call the desk... we will hold the tool for the next one', 'Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence'.
attributes.y_evidence: No folksy pull, but no visual lever carries neighbourly either: no place, people, photo of the room, the card or the tools; the type and colour are anonymous. Reflected in copy while the visuals say nothing.

attributes.x_evidence: Consistent 4px radius and borders; composed dark theme; precise copy and date formats; error states styled.
attributes.y_evidence: Craft lapses undercut 'careful': details list with two different label column widths; action bar button outside the content column; toast over the weekday header; basket session row orphan; done page still shows 'Basket (1)'; filters with native controls and misaligned labels.

The gap is the identity floor (ADR-035): name as a designed mark, imagery of the real tools and some material of the library's own world are allowed on Operate surfaces and are absent.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench placeholder instead of the tool
findings.description: All ten cards on the find page carry an identical wrench outline in a pale-green square where a picture of the tool would sit. The tile takes about a fifth of each card and carries no information; it reads as an unfilled placeholder.
findings.impact: Members recognise tools by sight ('the drill with two batteries'); identical tiles may slow scanning, and the visible placeholder makes the page look unfinished to first-time visitors.

evidence.detail: 10 of 10 cards use the same icon tile

findings.recommendation: Decide what each card shows of its tool: real photographs of the library's own stock, or a drawn device that differs per tool category; if neither is available, drop the tile rather than show a stand-in.

findings.title: No visual identity beyond the name set in bold body type
findings.description: The masthead is 'Fernhill Tool Library' in the body face at body weight-bold next to a stock wrench outline. No surface carries a mark, the membership-card green as a recognisable object, the community-centre room or any material from the library's world. The design.md rationale (green from the membership card) is not visible to a visitor.
findings.impact: Members may not recognise the page as their library's when arriving from a link, and 'neighbourly' is carried only by copy; the swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests all fail.
findings.recommendation: Decide which element of the library's own world (the membership card, the desk, the stock itself) becomes the identity floor on every page, and set the name as a designed mark that carries 'neighbourly, not folksy'.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar covers the calendar and sits outside the content column
findings.description: On the tool page the bottom action bar overlays the second week of the calendar (including the selected day in day-chosen) and its button is aligned to the window edge (x≈1264) while all content aligns to the 1120px column (right edge 1184).
findings.impact: Members may not see the day they just picked, and the misaligned button weakens the 'careful' attribute.
findings.recommendation: Decide how the bar and the calendar share the viewport (reserve space for the bar, or place the action in flow at wide widths) and align the bar's content to the page column.

findings.title: Basket sessions break into one full-width row and five cramped cells at 1280
findings.description: The six pick-up sessions render as Wed 28 Oct alone across the full width, then five narrow cards whose labels wrap to three lines ('Saturday 24 / October, 10:00 to / 13:00'). Order is newest first.
findings.impact: The odd first row may read as a recommended or different option, and the wrapped dates are harder to compare on the screen whose single job is choosing a session.
findings.recommendation: Decide one layout for the session list at wide widths in which every option has equal weight and the date reads on one line, in chronological order.

findings.title: Filters panel uses unthemed native date and select controls with misaligned labels
findings.description: The 'Available from' control shows the browser's 'yyyy/mm/dd' pattern and calendar glyph; the Category select is the native control; the Category label sits ~30px lower than 'Available from' because the hint text pushes alignment.
findings.impact: The date pattern contradicts the brief's 'Saturday 17 October' format members use, and the panel looks unfinished next to the themed search row.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the day filter should reuse the session-day vocabulary of the tool page, and align filter labels on one baseline.

findings.title: Tool details list uses two different label column widths
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from align values at x≈224, while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case align at x≈180, so the details block has two ragged value edges one above the other.
findings.impact: A visible misalignment on the page where members check the tool; it undercuts 'careful, not fussy'.
findings.recommendation: Treat the details as one list with one label column, or separate the two groups visibly.

findings.title: Find page at 375 puts search below all ten cards and truncates tool names
findings.description: At 375 the search field and filter button appear after the tenth card; card titles truncate ('Cordless drill 18 V, co...') so the two drills are indistinguishable; badges wrap 'Oct' alone; nav links wrap to two lines.
findings.impact: Phone is the main device; members may scroll past the whole list to search and cannot tell 'two batteries' from 'one battery' at a glance.
findings.recommendation: Decide the phone order from the job (find a tool) and let names wrap rather than truncate.

findings.title: Done and confirm pages leave the right half empty at wide widths
findings.description: At 1280 the 'What happens next' box and the confirm form fill about half the content width beside empty ground; the done page's lower third is empty and a grey band shows below the footer. The reservation number, what the member must remember, is plain body text in a table row.
findings.impact: The confirmation moment looks unfinished, and the details a member needs at the desk (number, session, deposit) do not stand out.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the member must carry to the desk and give it the page's focal point; size the layout to its content at wide widths.

findings.title: No-results state shows the full list with no empty-state message
findings.description: The no-results captures show 'sewing machine' in the search field and all ten tools listed, with no message. Either the empty state is missing or the capture did not submit; the state as captured is not designed.
findings.impact: Members searching for a tool the library lacks may believe the search failed or that listed tools match.

evidence.detail: no empty-state copy in any no-results capture

findings.recommendation: Verify the capture; if the state exists, design it to say what was searched and what to do next (e.g. ask the desk).

findings.title: Dark theme drops the badge fill only on 'available now' badges
findings.description: In dark mode, badges for tools available from Sat 10 Oct render as bare green text, while later-date badges keep a grey filled chip; in light mode both are filled. Detectors also measure these badges below 4.5:1 (A11Y-11).
findings.impact: The available-now signal, the most useful one on the page, is the weakest in dark mode, which many members use.
findings.recommendation: Compose the dark badge so the available-now state keeps at least the weight it has in light mode.

strengths: Volunteer voice in the copy: concrete, brief, kind ('returned when it comes back clean and working', 'we will hold the tool for the next one').
Deposit and availability date on every card; one filled action per page; a composed (not inverted) dark theme with consistent roles.
The pick-up calendar tagging session days 'Open' carries the library's real constraint.
keep: Keep the copy voice and the Open-session calendar mechanism; build the identity from the library's own world around them.
notes: No baseline in packet; pairwise not run. Detector output was not visible before the verdict file was written. Read anti-slop.md only after the verdict, to cite rule IDs.
